verdict.summary: Composio has no managed Clio Manage app, so you must register your own. That part is quick: start a free trial, create a Developer Application, and tick the permissions you need. Clio does not review private or unlisted apps. A review only applies if you want an App Directory listing, which takes a security questionnaire, a demo and a listing form. Watch two account issues: the trial lasts 7 days, and turning it into a free developer account needs Clio's approval, with no stated timeline.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min to connect your own account; 1-3 days of work for an optional App Directory listing (questionnaire, demo, listing copy)
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 30 min (trial signup plus app creation)
verdict.approval_wait: None for unlisted use. Converting a trial to a developer account has no stated timeline. An optional App Directory listing adds about 2 business days for security review, plus demo and listing turnaround.

gates.name: Trial / developer account with your own Developer Application
gates.unlocks: You can create a Clio Manage Developer Application and authorize your own Clio account through Composio.
limits: The trial account lasts 7 days. To keep building after that, apply for a free developer account; Clio reviews the application and gives no timeline.
Accounts and apps are tied to one region. You need a separate account (with a separate email) and a separate app for each of US, EU, CA and AU.
There is no separate sandbox. Your trial or developer account is the test environment.
Rate limit is 50 requests/min per access token at peak times. Custom increases are not offered.

gates.name: Private (unlisted) app
gates.unlocks: Users at other firms can authorize your app through the standard OAuth flow, each user individually. Clio has no test-user allowlist.
limits: Clio does not review private apps, and they cannot appear in the App Directory.
Creating apps requires access to a paid Clio account. Apps are not available on the EasyStart tier.
A user's granted permissions are fixed once they authorize. If you change permissions, users must re-authorize.
Access tokens last 30 days. Refresh tokens do not expire.
Clio documents no install cap or single-firm restriction for Manage apps. The single-firm rule applies to Clio Platform apps only.

gates.name: Clio App Directory listing
gates.unlocks: Your app is listed in the Clio App Directory and can be featured inside Clio Manage (App Integrations / 'Add to Clio'). Based on the docs, a listing is not required for other firms to authorize the app; it adds discoverability.
limits: Security and compliance questionnaire, delivered through OneTrust with MVSP as the baseline.
A demo to API Partnerships (pre-recorded per the current handbook).
The integration must support the latest two versions of Edge, Chrome, Firefox and Safari.
The listing name must not contain the word 'Clio'.
gates.time_to_reach: Days to weeks: about 2 business days for security review, plus the demo and listing turnaround

steps.title: Sign up for a Clio Manage trial in your region
steps.detail: Sign up for the free 7-day Clio Manage trial in the region where your integration will run (US app.clio.com, EU, CA or AU). Use this account to sign in to the Developer Portal.
gotchas: Each region needs its own trial, signed up with a separate email address.
Clio has no separate sandbox, so do not test on customer accounts.

steps.title: Apply for a free developer account
steps.detail: Before the 7-day trial ends, apply for a free developer account. Clio's team reviews the application and, if you are eligible, converts the trial into a developer account.
gotchas: Clio states no turnaround time, so apply on day one.
Private apps for real use require access to a paid Clio account.

steps.title: Choose the minimal access permissions
steps.detail: List the Clio API resources your agent actually uses. For each one, choose read-only or read/write, and keep the set as small as possible. Clio calls scopes 'access permissions'; they are set on the app itself, not passed in the authorize URL.
gotchas: Write access includes read, create, update and delete.
If you add permissions later, existing users must re-authorize to get them.

steps.title: Create the Developer Application
steps.detail: In developers.clio.com, go to Developer Apps and create an app. Fill in Name, Website URL and Redirect URIs, accept the Developer Terms of Service, and tick the App Permissions you chose. Description, Icons, Support URL and Deauthorization Callback URL are optional, but name, description, icon and website appear on the consent page.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The redirect_uri must exactly match one of the registered Redirect URIs.
Check which callback URL your Composio auth config actually shows before registering it.

steps.title: Add the client ID and secret to a Composio auth config
steps.detail: Copy the client ID and secret from developers.clio.com → Developer Apps → your app. Create a custom auth config for the clio_manage toolkit in Composio and paste them in. Leave the scope list empty, because permissions come from the Clio app.
gotchas: Composio's toolkit points to the US hosts (app.clio.com). EU, CA and AU firms need a regional app and regional hosts.
Clio sends the client secret in the POST body as form-urlencoded.

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start a Composio connection, sign in to your Clio trial, approve, and make a test API call. The authorization code expires after 10 minutes. Access tokens last 30 days and refresh tokens never expire.
gotchas: A 403 ForbiddenError means a permission is missing on the app.
The user's Clio role also limits what data they can see.

steps.title: Repeat for other regions if needed
steps.detail: If you serve firms in EU, CA or AU, create a Clio account and a Developer Application in each region's portal, and set up a matching Composio auth config that uses that region's hosts.

steps.title: Let users at other firms connect
steps.detail: Share the Composio connect flow with users at other firms. Each firm user authorizes the app separately. Clio does not review unlisted apps.
gotchas: Clio does not explicitly confirm production use by other firms without a listing; this is inferred from the docs.

steps.title: Request the security questionnaire (only if you want a listing)
steps.detail: Email api.partnerships@clio.com to request the security and compliance questionnaire. Complete it in OneTrust; it uses MVSP as the baseline.

steps.title: Wait for the security review
steps.detail: Clio's Application Security and Compliance team aims to review submissions within 2 business days. If you don't pass, they work with you on the gaps.

steps.title: Send a demo
steps.detail: After security approval, email api.partnerships@clio.com with a pre-recorded demo of your integration. The demo is used to assess UX, and the app must support the latest two versions of Edge, Chrome, Firefox and Safari.
gotchas: An older support article describes a booked 30-minute live demo instead. Ask API Partnerships which format they want.

steps.title: Submit the App Directory listing form
steps.detail: Draft and submit the listing form: a unique name without 'Clio', a short description of 10 words or fewer, a logo at least 300x300 px (transparent PNG or SVG) with no Clio logo, public Terms of Service and Privacy Policy URLs, a support contact, and your Application ID. API Partnerships drafts the listing for your sign-off and then publishes it.

requirements.item: Clio Manage trial or developer account in each region you serve
requirements.detail: The trial lasts 7 days. Convert it to a free developer account; Clio reviews the request. Use a separate email per region.

requirements.item: Developer Application with Name, Website URL, Redirect URIs, accepted Developer ToS and App Permissions
requirements.detail: These fields are required when creating the app.

requirements.item: Access to a paid Clio account (not EasyStart)
requirements.detail: Clio requires this to create private apps and get the key and secret. Apps are not available on the EasyStart tier.
Delivered through OneTrust with MVSP as the baseline; requested from api.partnerships@clio.com.
A demo for API Partnerships, and support for the latest two versions of Edge, Chrome, Firefox and Safari.
A name without 'Clio', a description of 10 words or fewer, a logo of at least 300x300 px (PNG or SVG), a public Terms of Service, a public Privacy Policy, a support contact and the Application ID.

scopes.scope: Access permissions (per resource, read-only or read/write)
scopes.effect: Selected as checkboxes on the Developer Application, not in the authorize URL. No permission triggers a separate review. Existing users keep the permissions they originally granted until they re-authorize.

blockers.symptom: Developer account access ends after 7 days
blockers.cause: The trial account expires, and conversion to a developer account needs Clio's approval.
blockers.fix: Apply for the free developer account right after signing up for the trial.

blockers.symptom: 403 ForbiddenError, or redacted associations in API responses
blockers.cause: The app lacks the permission, or the user authorized before you added it. The user's Clio role can also restrict data.
blockers.fix: Add the permission on the Developer Application and have users re-authorize. Check the user's role in Clio.

blockers.cause: Apps and accounts are region-specific, and Composio's toolkit uses US hosts.
blockers.fix: Create an app in the regional portal and point a Composio auth config at that region's hosts.

blockers.cause: The redirect_uri must match a registered Redirect URI exactly.
blockers.fix: Register the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config.

blockers.cause: The per-token limit is 50 requests/min at peak times, and custom increases are not supported.
blockers.fix: Respect the Retry-After header and spread out requests.

blockers.cause: Apps are not available on the EasyStart pricing tier.
blockers.fix: The firm needs a higher Clio plan.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Clio Manage, so you always need your own Developer Application from developers.clio.com. Leave scopes empty in Composio, because permissions are set on the Clio app. The toolkit uses the US endpoints (app.clio.com/oauth/authorize and /oauth/token); other regions need their own app and regional hosts. Register the exact callback URL your Composio auth config shows. The toolkit default and the callback seen in testing differed.

evidence.claim: Composio toolkit clio_manage exists but has no managed OAuth. It uses OAUTH2 with app.clio.com authorize/token URLs and empty default scopes.
Clio Manage apps are created at developers.clio.com, separate from the Clio Platform portal.
evidence.quote: The Clio Manage developer portal is located at https://developers.clio.com and is the location for creating your Clio Manage OAuth Applications.

evidence.claim: A free 7-day trial in each region is a prerequisite. Client id and secret are under Developer Apps.
evidence.quote: This trial account will be active for 7 days. You must sign up for the trial in the region(s) in which your integration will operate.

evidence.claim: Clio reviews applications to convert a trial into a developer account.
evidence.quote: Our team will review the application and, if eligible, your trial account will be converted to a developer account.

evidence.claim: Clio has no separate sandbox.
evidence.quote: Clio does not have a separate sandbox environment.

evidence.claim: Required Developer Application fields are Name, Website URL, Redirect URIs, Developer ToS acceptance and App Permissions.
evidence.quote: One or more URLs to which the user will be redirected after they complete the OAuth authorization flow.

evidence.claim: Multi-region apps need a Clio account and Developer Application in each region.
evidence.quote: If your app operates in multiple Clio regions, you will need a Clio account and Developer Application in each region.

evidence.claim: The API exists in four regions: US, EU, CA and AU.
evidence.quote: The API is available in four distinct data regions: Australia (au.app.clio.com), Canada (ca.app.clio.com), EU (eu.app.clio.com) and US (app.clio.com).

evidence.claim: Only the authorization code grant is supported, and the redirect_uri must match a registered one. No scope parameter is documented.
evidence.quote: The URL must match one of the redirect URLs specified in your application settings.

evidence.claim: The authorization code is valid for 10 minutes. The token exchange is a form-urlencoded POST with the client secret in the body.
evidence.quote: Note that this request must specify the `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` content-type in an HTTP header.

evidence.claim: Access tokens last 30 days, and refresh tokens do not expire.
evidence.quote: Refresh tokens do not expire; as a result, they should be encrypted and stored securely.

evidence.claim: Scopes are 'access permissions' selected on the app, each as read-only or read/write.
evidence.quote: this concept is interchangable with that of OAuth scopes

evidence.claim: Existing user grants stay fixed until the user re-authorizes. Missing scopes return 403.
evidence.quote: once a user has authorized your application, their permissions are fixed, even if their token is refreshed

evidence.claim: No sensitive scope tier was found. The user's Clio role also limits data access.
evidence.quote: Even with the correct OAuth scope, a user can only access data their Clio role permits.

evidence.claim: Clio's API is open, with no approvals needed to start building.
evidence.quote: Clio offers an open API, so anyone can build on it and there are no approvals or gates preventing you from getting started today.

evidence.claim: Private Manage apps are not reviewed, cannot be listed, require a paid account, and are not available on EasyStart.
evidence.quote: Private apps for Clio Manage are not reviewed by Clio and cannot be published in Clio's App Directory. You will need access to a paid Clio account to create apps and get your app key and secret.

evidence.claim: The single-firm restriction applies to Clio Platform apps. No equivalent is stated for Manage apps.
evidence.quote: Apps built in the Clio Platform developer portal start as private by default and can only be authorized by users of a single Clio firm/account at a time.

evidence.claim: To start an App Directory launch, email api.partnerships@clio.com for the security questionnaire.
evidence.quote: To request a security questionnaire, email our API Partnerships team at api.partnerships@clio.com

evidence.claim: The questionnaire is delivered through OneTrust on an MVSP baseline, with a target review time of 2 business days.
evidence.quote: We aim to review submissions within 2 business days.

evidence.claim: After security approval, send a pre-recorded demo. The app must support the latest two versions of major browsers.
evidence.quote: send an email to our API Partnerships team (api.partnerships@clio.com) with a pre-recorded demo

evidence.claim: After the demo, you fill in the listing form, and API Partnerships drafts and publishes the listing.
Listing requirements include a name without 'Clio', a short description, a logo, ToS, a Privacy Policy, a support contact and the Application ID.
evidence.quote: The app name must not contain the word "Clio".

evidence.claim: Featuring an app inside Clio Manage requires an App Directory listing or approval to be listed.
evidence.quote: your app must either be either listed on the Clio App Directory already, or you’ve been approved to be listed

evidence.claim: The rate limit is 50 requests/min per token at peak, with no custom increases.
evidence.quote: We do not support custom rate limit increases for applications at this time.

evidence.claim: developers.clio.com is live behind a Clio login.
Register the Composio callback as a Redirect URI on the Clio app, but confirm which callback URL your auth config uses.
An unlisted Manage app can probably be authorized by any non-EasyStart Clio user. A listing appears to be needed only for discoverability.

open_questions: Can an unlisted, unreviewed Manage app be used in production by users at other paying firms? This is inferred, not stated by Clio.
How long does Clio take to convert a trial into a free developer account?
Which Composio callback URL should be registered: v1 auth-apps/add (the toolkit default) or v3 toolkits/auth/callback?
What are the Redirect URI rules beyond exact match: is HTTPS required, and are localhost or wildcards allowed?
Is PKCE supported? It is not mentioned in the docs.
Are refresh tokens rotated on refresh? The sample response shows no new refresh_token.
Is the demo a live 30-minute call or a pre-recorded video? The current handbook and the older support article disagree.
Is a scope parameter on the authorize URL ignored or rejected?
